title: Aurora manual failover runbook
brief: Can you turn this into a proper runbook page for the Database Reliability team at Fenwick Bank? It covers a manual failover of the orders-aurora-prod Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. Section titled "When to use this runbook": use it when the writer instance has been unhealthy for more than 5 minutes and automatic failover has not happened, or for a planned failover during the Sunday maintenance window (02:00 to 04:00 UTC). Section titled "Prerequisites" as a bulleted list: the break-glass role db-failover-operator, access to the #db-incidents channel, and the replica lag dashboard open. Section titled "Failover steps" as a numbered list: 1 announce the failover in #db-incidents; 2 confirm replica lag on the target reader is under 30 seconds; 3 put the orders service into read-only mode with the feature flag orders.readonly; 4 trigger the failover to reader instance orders-aurora-prod-r2; 5 wait for the cluster endpoint to point at the new writer (usually 30 to 60 seconds); 6 turn orders.readonly off; 7 watch the connection count recover to its normal level of about 400. Put a prominent warning before step 4: never fail over to a reader whose lag exceeds 30 seconds, because committed orders will be lost. Section titled "Verification": a short table with columns Check, Expected: Writer instance, orders-aurora-prod-r2; Replica lag, under 1 second; Error rate on orders API, under 0.5 percent; Connections, about 400. Section titled "Rollback": one paragraph saying that if the new writer is unhealthy, fail back to orders-aurora-prod-r1 using the same steps, and escalate to the on-call DBA lead.

edit.request: Lower the replica lag threshold from 30 seconds to 20 seconds in the steps and the warning, and add a new step right after enabling read-only mode: "Pause the nightly-reconcile job".
